subject: CAIQ control ledger and ephemeral log samples
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@terrahealth.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security@terrahealth.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ mapping request — ephemeral logs and control ledger

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for walking us through the platform yesterday. As we prepare our internal review, the security team has asked for two focused artifacts to finish the CAIQ mapping: a control ledger that maps each CAIQ question to Redwood controls and owners, and a small sample of ephemeral KV/prefix cache logs (anonymized) to validate the runtime retention and access patterns.

Can you provide:
- A control ledger (spreadsheet) that includes CAIQ control IDs, Redwood assertion text, control owner, evidence filename(s), and a short confidence note.
- A sanitized log sample (ndjson or similar) showing a short-lived KV cache lifecycle across a few requests (timestamped, redacted IDs).

Also helpful: a one-page snippet of the retention policy that governs ephemeral caches and how long we expect KV entries to live in the hosted product.

Targeting our vendor review next Tuesday (2027-04-06). Does that timeline work? If possible, we’d like the files by end of day Monday so our reviewers have time to ingest.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call if that helps.

--
Alice Morgan
Security Program Manager
TerraHealth
From: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@terrahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ mapping request — ephemeral logs and control ledger

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver the control ledger and sanitized log sample on Monday EOD (2027-04-05 PDT). Quick notes on scope and owners:

- Owner for the control ledger: Kimberly Park (compliance PM) will own content/format and mapping decisions.
- Log sample and retention snippet: Marissa Cole (Security Ops) will provide the ndjson extract and the retention PDF excerpt.
- I’ll assemble the ZIP and include a short readme that ties each ledger row to the exact artifact filename and any sampling caveats.

Couple of clarifying questions so we scope redaction correctly:
1) For the KV/cache sample, do you want full request/response latencies included, or only timestamps and event types?
2) Any specific PII/PHI redaction rules beyond replacing customer IDs with deterministic hashes?

If you’re OK, we’ll produce a compact ledger (one sheet per CAIQ domain) and a 50–200-line ndjson sample with IDs hashed and IPs redacted.

I’m looping Kimberly and Marissa to confirm timing.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Security & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@terrahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ mapping request — ephemeral logs and control ledger

Hi all — confirming we’ll deliver Monday EOD. Delivery plan below: 

1) CAIQ_Control_Ledger_v1.2.xlsx — columns: CAIQ_ID | Assertion | Redwood_Control_Text | Owner | Evidence_File | Confidence_Level | Notes. I added a Confidence_Level (High/Med/Low) to flag assertions that require a runbook or live demo.

2) kv_cache_log_sample_20270301.ndjson — 150-line sample, UUIDs hashed, IPs removed, latencies preserved. We’ll include event types: cache_set, cache_get, cache_eviction and a timestamp + shard id to show distribution.

3) retention_policy_snippet.pdf — one page excerpt from our runtime retention policy describing ephemeral KV TTLs (default 2 minutes, configurable per-customer up to 30 minutes for dedicated tenants) and admin access controls.

Attachments: will be delivered as a single ZIP with a README that maps ledger rows to files and notes sampling caveats. If TerraHealth needs log samples in a different format (CSV) let me know.

Jonas — tagging you for the canonical archive location and proof-of-possession note for audit traceability. Can you generate the Drive link and HS ticket reference once uploaded?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@terrahealth.com>
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ mapping request — ephemeral logs and control ledger

Alice — attaching the artifacts here (see filenames below). The ndjson sample has been sanitized per the rules we discussed: identifiers hashed with a prefix so routes can be traced in the sample without exposing customer IDs. Please confirm receipt and let us know if you want the sample expanded to include a few synthetic long-tail eviction events.

Attachments:
- CAIQ_Control_Ledger_v1.2.xlsx (xlsx) — single-sheet index per CAIQ domain, ledger rows reference evidence filenames.
- kv_cache_log_sample_20270301.ndjson (ndjson) — 150 lines, events include cache_set/cache_get/cache_eviction, timestamps in RFC3339.
- retention_policy_snippet.pdf (pdf) — excerpt showing default TTL and admin escalation flow.

We’ve also uploaded an archived bundle to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-terrahealth-caiq and created HubSpot ticket HS-23459 for audit tracking.

If everything looks good, we can schedule a 20-min walkthrough Monday morning to step through anything the reviewers flag before your Tuesday window.

—Marissa Cole
Security Ops Specialist
Redwood Inference
